title: My Nightmare Bulk (Story Time)
summary: NH tells how, after five years of slow, unplanned gaining at home, he discovered YouTube fitness and powerlifting and force-fed himself from about 180 lb to 230-240 lb. The dirty bulk wrecked his conditioning, calisthenics, volume, physique balance and health, left him injured and barely able to walk, and still feeds his bigorexia. He gives rules to keep a bulk honest.
claims: For his first 5 years he simply ate what his parents served and followed his appetite, going from 110 to about 160-170 lb without ever cutting
Beginners don't need perfect macros: a balanced diet with enough calories guarantees muscle gain
Unless you are fat or obese, don't cut during your first ~5 years of training; you haven't built anything to reveal yet
He sped up his bulk without any reason: he was still progressing and not plateaued, so raising the surplus was his first mistake
Judge a monthly weight gain as a percentage of bodyweight; at 180 lb, several pounds a month is far too much to be muscle for an intermediate or advanced lifter
Fast weight gain can be justified only for true beginners filling out their frame, not for intermediates
If strength rises only in proportion to weight gained (e.g. +20 lb bench for +10 lb bodyweight), it's a bad trade and mostly not muscle
Building fat is easy because the body wants reserves; muscle is hard-won tissue. Fat is lazy tissue, muscle is struggle tissue
'Bulking hypnosis': the instant gratification of a bulk blinds you to how fat you are getting
People overestimate their leanness; they plan a 20 lb cut and discover they need to lose 40-60 lb
He hid his fat gain from himself with baggy clothes and by dropping calisthenics he was getting bad at
Never abandon calisthenics on a bulk: being able to move your body with ease reveals the truth about what you are gaining
Bulk test: compare push-up and pull-up numbers with bench numbers; if bench rises while push-ups/pull-ups drop a lot, slow down or stop the bulk
Getting fat damaged his conditioning, so he drifted from 6-10 and 8-12 reps toward 3x5s and singles, not because they were better but because they were all he could do
A bulk should increase work capacity and volume; if volume regresses on a bulk, why bulk at all? The extra calories should serve your training
His sessions got shorter and he skipped isolation for the big three, which gave him a spider physique with lagging arms
He gained 20-30 lb in about one year, reaching 200 lb, which was far too much
Never set a goal bodyweight on a bulk; it becomes an obsession and you bulk just to hit the number
Strength standards like a 3-plate bench can keep a bodybuilder's chest small, because the training to reach them doesn't align with hypertrophy; goals must align with what you actually want
Every morning he ate 12 eggs on six toasts soaked in oil and butter; nobody needs 12 eggs a day, the excess can't be used and only makes you fat
He ate cheap low-quality eggs and almost no vegetables during that bulk
Every Saturday he force-fed a pound of pasta bolognese in one evening while watching pro-bodybuilder motivation videos, not realising the pros grew from drugs, not from eating
You can't turn unlimited calories into muscle; your protein synthesis is limited, but your capacity to get fat is not
If you have to force-feed and hate your food, the bulk will fail; misery is not being hardcore
The dirty bulk about five years ago gave him lasting body dysmorphia (bigorexia): he still feels not big enough
Unbalanced macros, no micronutrients and random minimalist training led to constant injuries that would not heal
He broke a rib squatting about four plates, weakened by allergy sneezing, and it wouldn't heal under 230-240 lb of bodyweight
At 240 lb, aged 23-24, he could barely walk 10 minutes on a Chicago trip without rib pain and swollen ankles, which made him start his only cut
Squatting to the grass isn't functional; being functional means moving well, being healthy and enjoying life with your family
Natural bodybuilding is health first; a good-looking body done properly is also a healthy body
A properly planned bulk boosts performance, allows more volume and blows up your physique
exercises: a drop alongside bench gains signals you are gaining fat, not muscle
training_log: about four plates; broke a rib
